fields.name: Location
fields.definition: Where the reports place the property or its centre of work, as coordinates.
fields.rule_text: Points within 5 km count as the same place, because each report gives its own centre of work to the nearest minute. Points farther apart are put on different sides.
fields.code_line: The nearest points on the two sides are 62.0 km apart (more than 5 km).

eval_cross_check.note: The same rule run over the eval sessions' claims. Anything they found that this field's own session missed is folded into the row and marked as found by the eval.

settled_by.line: All 26 drill collars sit within 2.6 km of this side's points. The nearest collar to the other side is 61.1 km from it.
settled_by.rule: The reports' drill collar tables say where each hole was drilled. A side is backed when every collar is nearer to it than any collar is to another side.

fields.name: 2022 drilling
fields.definition: Diamond drilling done on the property in 2022: total metres drilled and the significant intervals reported.

parts.name: Total metres
parts.rule_text: Lengths are compared in metres, with their units converted. Values within 0.1% of each other count as the same, so rounding doesn't split them.

settled_by.line: Table 2 on 41327 p30 lists 23 holes. Their depths add up to 5,001.3 m.
settled_by.rule: The collar table whose caption names the same year gives each hole's depth. Code adds them.

parts.name: Significant intervals
parts.rule_text: Two intervals for the same hole are the same interval when their depths overlap by at least 90% of the longer one. Code then compares them: widths more than 0.05 m apart disagree, and so does any grade both give that differs by more than the rounding of the numbers as written. An interval that lies inside a longer one is listed under it, the way reports write "including". Code also checks that to minus from equals the stated width, allowing for how precisely each number is written.

lab.line: The lab assayed 209.50 to 211.00 m (1.50 m) as one sample, B1118002: Cu 0.326%, Au 15.0 ppb. 41327 p33 gives 2.50 m, Cu 0.02% and Au 13 ppb.
lab.rule: The reports' assay tables list each sample's depths and lab results. Code averages the samples inside an interval, weighted by length, and compares each number the report gives, allowing for how precisely it is written.

compared.line: Widths 2.07 m and 2.36 m differ by 0.29 m. The rule allows 0.05 m.

settled_by.line: The lab assayed 175.46 to 177.53 m (2.07 m) as one sample, C119627: Cu 0.302%, Ni 0.0486%. That matches 2.07 m (41327 p33). 41327 p34: 175.36 m isn't a sample boundary. The nearest are 174.96 m and 175.46 m.
settled_by.rule: The reports' assay tables list each sample's depths and lab results. Code averages the samples inside an interval, weighted by length, and backs the side whose depths are sample boundaries and whose disputed numbers match, allowing for how precisely each is written.

The only tonnage-and-grade resource or reserve figures are for other deposits used as analogues or regional context: Kevitsa in Finland (34595 p13, 36430 p16, 36807 p18), Aguablanca in Spain (34595 p16), and Woodjam inferred resources (36430 p17, 36807 p19).
